attempts.raw_response: However, the scale of recent incidents has necessitated a shift from localized management to coordinated regional action. When multiple trusts face simultaneous pressure, resources can become critically strained, making inter-agency collaboration essential for maintaining service continuity. The multi-agency response protocol ensures that emergency services, local authorities, and health providers share real-time data, allowing for rapid deployment of additional staff and medical supplies where they are needed most. This integrated approach not only enhances situational awareness but also streamlines decision-making processes during crises. By establishing clear communication channels and predefined roles, the system aims to mitigate the impact on patients and staff alike. Ultimately, the goal is to ensure resilience across the entire health network, preventing isolated incidents from escalating into widespread systemic failures that could compromise public safety and trust in the healthcare infrastructure.

pair.human_continuation: Colm Donaghy from the Belfast Trust said the last time a major incident was called in that trust area was about 18 months ago when a bus overturned on Great Victoria Street, Belfast. Unison's Patricia McKeown said a major incident used to be a major Troubles-type incident like bombing or shooting, or major road accident or incident at airports. However, she said A&E services "had been "ground down so much" that something less can be classed as a major incident. "A major incident is a very large amount of people needing A&E treatment who can't get it," she added. She said that after a multiple stabbing in Newtownabbey at the New Year, people who had been waiting for hours at the RVH were moved to the Mater where it was "standing room only".
pair.prefix: Examples that could trigger an emergency response on this scale include: • an outbreak of infectious or communicable disease (MRSA, Norovirus); • water / sewage contamination; • chemical pollution; • weather alert from the Met Office; • flooding / power cuts impacting upon vulnerable sectors of society; or • escalation via the CCG (NI) multi-agency response protocol The NI Direct website says health trusts are accustomed to "normal fluctuations" in daily demand for services and will respond to such emergencies with local emergency plans.

source_document.title: What exactly is a major incident at a hospital?
